condition: Breast cancer screening — average risk, age 40–49
summary: 42-year-old asymptomatic woman at a wellness visit, never had a mammogram, no family history. USPSTF 2024: biennial mammography from 40 to 74.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Wellness check — asks when to start mammograms
inputs.hpi: Asymptomatic 42-year-old woman at a wellness visit. Has never had a mammogram and asks when she should start and how often. No breast lumps, no nipple discharge, no skin change. No family history of breast or ovarian cancer. Last cervical screening test 2 years ago, normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Breast screening — average risk, age 42
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic, average risk, normal examination. Screening mammography every 2 years from 40.

mustNotAlarm.note: An asymptomatic screening visit must not raise an "emergency now" banner (alarm fatigue; front desk would redirect a well person).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: computeClinicalPrompts preventative prompts are fixed age/sex rules: mammogram_check says 'Annual mammogram recommended from age 40' and '> 1 year for 40–49' (USPSTF 2024: biennial 40–74).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Change the mammogram_check rationale/interval to biennial for 40–74.

mustExclude.note: No symptom: no diagnostic breast pathway.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for breast cancer
guideline.section: Biennial screening mammography for women aged 40–74 (grade B)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for breast cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2024;331:1918–1930.

rationale: USPSTF 2024 moved the start of average-risk breast screening to 40 with a biennial interval. A screening request needs no diagnostic (triple-assessment) pathway.

authoring.author: Claude (prevention/screening, obstetric-gynaecological mimics and paediatric surgery cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Every citation is verified: false. iOS outcomes are unverified (not run on Linux); triage after the first CI run.
